newsitem.title: GERMANY: MEXICO TO BUY OILS/FATS DUE TO LOW STOCK - OIL WORLD.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO TO BUY OILS/FATS DUE TO LOW STOCK - OIL WORLD.

text.p: Mexico is likely to become an active buyer of oils and fats in the world market in the next few months, the independent Oil World newsletter said on Tuesday.
It cited extremely low stocks and a moderate rise in domestic consumption.
Oils and fats stocks on July 1, 1997 were at 116,000 tonnes, down from 139,000 tonnes in January 1997 and 177,000 tonnes on July 1, 1996.
They represented less than one month of usage.
Mexico had already bought 20,000 tonnes of sun oil from Argentina earlier this month and soybean oil would also be required in July/September, Oil World said.
Mexico reduced its oil and meal imports earlier this year because it stepped up its domestic soybean crushings but it was still likely to return to the world market for imports.
Oil World data showed October/May 1996/97 oilseeds imports at 2.60 million tonnes versus 2.39 million in the same period of 1995/96.
Oils/fats imports in the eight months had declined to 572,700 tonnes from 602,900 a year earlier.
Oilmeal imports had more than halved to 180,200 tonnes (463,600) because the meal-driven soya crush from imported beans generated more domestic meal.
